issue.title: Frustum culling when parent mesh is scaled
issue.body:
This is a slightly modified version of gero3's proposal for issue #448 at:

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/448#issuecomment-1887476

It's the trivial solution. Do you think it will be cheaper to lazily update the child meshes upon scaling operations on their parents? I'm not sure if the trade off in performance and complexity will be beneficial.

If there are any conventions or guidelines I missed - please correct me.

body: It seems a little bit overkill to me. If I'm not mistaken the longest the hierarchy the more complex the calculation. I think it'll be better to have something like `.scaleWorld` that just applies the parent scale to the current object.

Come to think of it, assuming that the `.matrixWorld` of the object is updated we should be able to extract the scale factors from it with `.matrixWorld.decompose()[2]`. This will simplify the operation to O(1) for any hierarchy. I tested it, and it checks out. In fact, we can micro-optimize it further and extract the scale factors specifically without the use of `.decompose()`

You can see an example of the fix here: 
http://jsfiddle.net/5kPaA/

@mrdoob, what do you think? Is it safe enough to assume that the `.matrixWorld` is updated for frustum evaluation? Am I missing something?

issue.title: Frustum culling when the parent mesh is scaled
issue.body:
Another attempt at #448, following @mrdoob's guidance at  https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/448#issuecomment-3331280

The main difference is the use of `.matrix.getColumnX()` (and equivalents) for:
- Using an existing interface
- Column getters are optimized to avoid the overhead of Vector3 instantiation
- Keep the code concise.

issue.title: Ray intersection fails when Mesh parent is scaled
issue.body:
This is a nearly identical problem as was fixed for [#448](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/448):

When a Mesh ancestor is scaled, the ray intersection test does not take this scaling into account when checking for intersection with the bounding sphere (only the mesh scaling is used):

``` javascript
if ( distance > object.geometry.boundingSphere.radius * Math.max( object.scale.x, Math.max( object.scale.y, object.scale.z ) ) )
```

I verified that this is the problem in my application by manually scaling all of the bounding spheres in the hierarchy, and after doing this, ray intersection worked perfectly.  

Perhaps a solution similar to #448 will work with minimal impact?
